transcript.text: t/d keeps cutting out after 10 mins then starts again if i leave it. vent hose goes out the window. pls help

That sounds like your tumble dryer is overheating. Most dryers have a thermal cut-out that switches the heater or the whole machine off when it gets too hot, then resets once it cools down. That's why it starts again if you leave it. The usual cause is poor airflow, and with a hose out the window, that's the first suspect.

## Check these first (most likely fixes)

1. Lint filter
• Pull it out and clean it properly. If it looks clean but feels "waxy" (common with fabric softener), wash it in warm soapy water, rinse, and let it dry fully.
• Clean the slot the filter sits in. A vacuum crevice tool works well. Fluff often builds up behind it.

2. Vent hose
• Kinks or squashing: Is it pinched where the window closes on it? Even a partly crushed hose can cause this.
• Length and bends: Keep it as short and straight as possible. Long hoses (over ~2 m) or loops and dips trap hot air and moisture.
• Blockage: Disconnect it and look or shake through it. Fluff and damp lint collect inside, especially in dips.
• Outside end: Make sure nothing blocks the end, such as a flap stuck shut, a bush or the hose dropping into a corner.
• Test: Run the dryer for 10–15 minutes with the hose disconnected (window open, room ventilated). If it no longer cuts out, the hose is the problem. Replacing it is cheap.

3. Space around the dryer
• Leave a gap behind and around it so it can breathe. Don't run it in a tiny closed cupboard.

4. Load
• Don't overload it, and spin clothes well in the washer first. Very wet, heavy loads make it work harder.

## If that doesn't fix it

These are internal faults:
• Lint build-up inside the machine (behind the filter housing or in the internal ducting)
• Faulty fan or fan belt
• Failing thermostat or thermal cut-out (may trip too early)
• Heater element problems

These usually mean taking panels off, so unplug it first. If you're not comfortable doing that, call a repair person.

## ⚠️ Safety

• Don't keep running it while it's repeatedly cutting out. Overheating plus lint is a real fire risk.
• Never leave it running while you're out or asleep until it's fixed.
• If you smell burning or the casing is very hot to touch, stop using it and get it checked.
• Check the model number for recalls (some UK dryers had fire-risk recalls).

its an indesit, label inside door says IDV 75. it stops completely, drum stops but light stays on. cabinet gets really hot before it stops

## ⚠️ Important first: check if your dryer is part of the safety recall

Many Indesit vented dryers, including IDV75 models, were included in the Whirlpool/Indesit tumble dryer fire-risk recall. The problem is that lint can build up and touch the heating element, which is a fire risk. A cabinet getting very hot and the machine cutting out matches that risk.

Please stop using it until you've checked:

1. Unplug it.
2. Find the serial number on the label inside the door (near where you found "IDV 75").
3. Search "Whirlpool tumble dryer recall" for the official safety-check page, or call Whirlpool/Indesit customer support, and enter or give them the model and serial number.
4. If it's affected and hasn't been modified, they should fix or replace it free.

## What's likely happening

The drum stopping while the light stays on means power is still on, but something has cut the motor. Usually that's a thermal protector tripping from overheating, then resetting once it cools. That's why it starts again later.

Common causes on this model:

• Lint build-up inside the machine (very common on IDV75s): fluff collects behind the filter housing, in the fan housing, and around the heater and motor, so hot air can't escape.
• Motor working too hard: worn drum bearing, rollers or belt causing drag makes the motor overheat.
• Blocked or restricted vent hose (see my earlier checks).

## Quick checks you can do safely

• Turn the drum by hand (unplugged). It should turn fairly smoothly. Stiff, grinding or squeaking points to bearings or rollers.
• Run it on a cool/no-heat setting for 15–20 minutes, only if the recall check comes back clear.
• Still stops? The motor is overheating (drag or a motor fault).
• Only stops on heat? It's an airflow or lint problem.
• Look into the filter slot with a torch. Thick fluff in there usually means more deeper inside.

## Next step

Cleaning out the internal lint means removing the back or front panel. It's doable if you're handy (unplug first), but given the fire-risk history of this model, a recall check or engineer visit is the better route. If it's not covered by the recall and the machine is old, weigh repair cost against replacing it.

its my landlords dryer so ill need to tell him. i checked the hose tho, its crushed behind the dryer where i pushed it back, and with it off the window it ran the whole 40 mins no cutting out. is that the problem?

Yes, that's almost certainly the cause. A crushed hose traps the hot, damp air, the dryer overheats, and the thermal cut-out stops it. Running the full 40 minutes once the hose was freed is a clear result.

## What to do now

1. Fix the hose
• Check it for damage. If it's split, flattened for good, or stays kinked, replace it. Universal dryer vent hoses are cheap (usually 4 inch / 100 mm) at hardware shops or online.
• Leave a gap behind the dryer so the hose doesn't get squashed when you push the machine back. Leaving it slightly pulled out from the wall is usually enough.
• Keep the run short and straight to the window, with no dips or loops.

2. Still check the recall
Even with the cause found, please do the serial number check (see my earlier steps) before using it regularly. The IDV75 recall is about lint inside the machine touching the heater, and running hot repeatedly can make that worse. It's free, takes a few minutes, and as the landlord's dryer it's his responsibility to sort out if it's affected.

3. Tell your landlord
You could send something like:

> Hi, the tumble dryer (Indesit IDV75) kept cutting out from overheating. I found the vent hose was crushed behind it, and it works fine with the hose freed. The hose may need replacing. Also, this model was part of the Whirlpool/Indesit fire safety recall. Could you check whether this one has been modified? The serial number is on the label inside the door.

## Going forward
• Clean the lint filter after every load.
• If it starts cutting out again, or smells of burning, stop using it and let your landlord know.
